c.tagline: The Marianas' laid-back main island — turquoise dive sites, WWII history, and endless summer.

taxi.fareNote: No ride-hailing apps operate on Saipan. Getting around means metered or flat-rate taxis (airport to Garapan runs about $20-30, though many hotels offer a cheaper flat shuttle) or — by far the most practical option — a rental car.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number, as on the US mainland; the Commonwealth Health Center in Garapan is the island's main hospital.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.San Antonio: San Antonio Saipan Coral Ocean Resort

avoid.reason: Car break-ins happen at quiet beach parks and viewpoints, so leave nothing in rental cars, and watch for stray dogs on back roads.

hood_desc: The island's tourist heart on the west coast: the main strip of hotels, restaurants, bars, and duty-free shops backing onto Micro Beach and American Memorial Park — the base for most visitors.
The adjoining administrative and local-life districts wrapped around Saipan's calm western lagoon, with the courts, sugar-dock beaches, and everyday shops; quieter and more residential than Garapan.
A southern residential village near the airport and the reef-fringed south coast, home to Coral Ocean Resort and its golf course; low-key and convenient for arrivals.
The breezy hillside seat of the CNMI government above Garapan, with Japanese-era ruins and cooler air; residential and green, a quiet base with a car.
The wild northern tip of the island, uninhabited apart from its sights: Banzai Cliff, the Last Command Post, Bird Island lookout, and the world-famous Grotto dive site.

water.note: Island tap water is often brackish and not reliably potable; drink bottled water.

transit.hours: Public transport is minimal; a limited shuttle serves some routes during the day. Most visitors rely on rental cars or taxis.
transit.note: Saipan has no real public transit system beyond a limited shuttle plus hotel and tour shuttles. A rental car is the standard way to get around; taxis are available but pricey.
transit.pay: Taxis are paid in cash or by card in US dollars; there is no transit-card system. Rental cars are widely available at the airport and in Garapan.

ferry: Managaha Island transfer boats from Garapan

transit.m: Hotel shuttle to Garapan (flat rate, often ~$10 per person)

tip.r: US-style tipping: ~15-20% at restaurants and for taxis and guides.
